newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper market looks weak, eyes stocks.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper market looks weak, eyes stocks.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper is vulnerable to further easing towards interim support around $1,915, with little on the technical horizon suggesting strength, analysts said.
Copper stocks at London Metal Exchange warehouses are expected to fall by around 5,000 tonnes, which could provide a small boost to prices, some traders said.
COPPER - Prices were expected to continue drifting lower in the absence of technical upward momentum, analysts said.
"A breach of $1,917 would break a nearby support trendline and a move below the recent low $1,905 would confirm further weakness," analyst William Adams of Rudolf Wolff said in a commentary.
The RSI continued to trend lower and prices were trading below slightly falling moving averages, analysts said.
A drop in stocks could offer a bit of support to the market. "But a bearish stock report could be the catalyst for another sell-off," Adams noted.
However, a flag formation may be appearing on the charts, which would indicate a push up towards at least the $1,940 area before retracing towards $1,800-$1,850, one dealer said.
But that would not be apparent until the end of the week.
Important resistance remained in the $1,970-$1,980 band.
At 0745 GMT three months LME copper was quoted at $1,925/30, up $4 from Friday's late close.
ALUMINIUM - Like copper, prices are trending lower and appear increasingly vulnerable to a test of the $1,470 support level.
A breach of that level would target $1,454, analysts said.
"Techcnially, a rather weak picture with a continued steep fall of the RSI along with prices stil trading below the moving averages," said brokers Brandeis.
At 0745 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1471/73, down $5 from Monday's late close.
